star_system.skill_level_unlocks: Skill Lv1 at 0 stars (just owning the character), Skill Lv2 at 2 stars, Skill Lv3 at 5 stars, Skill Lv4 at 7 stars. Skill level is separate from star/character level.
star_system.note: Stars 1, 4, and 7 give the same stat boost per character (e.g. Alex gets [All] Max HP +3% each time). Stars 3 and 6 each unlock a resonance slot. Star 7 gives both a stat boost AND skill level 4.

resonance.description: Resonance allows characters to equip skills from other characters you own.
resonance.unlock_at: Star 3 (+1 slot) and Star 6 (+1 slot, 2 total)
resonance.how_it_works: A 6-star character can equip 2 borrowed skills from other characters in addition to their own skill. The borrowed skill uses the level from the character who owns it.
resonance.example: A 6-star Dracoola can equip Hou Yi's Sun Piercer and Nyanja's Cloudfooted if you own those characters.
resonance.pvp_note: Phynx's Desert Tribunal is widely considered the best resonance skill for PvP.

best_resonance_combos.description: PvP resonance pairings ranked by effectiveness. Resonance requires characters at 3-star (1 slot) or 6-star (2 slots).

s_tier_p2p.note: Best PvP resonance combo in the game. Phynx bleeds stack with Cleo's fire marks for devastating damage. Expensive to build — both are epic/legendary and need high star levels.

a_tier_f2p.note: Strong F2P option. Helix does more damage as he takes damage, and Phynx adds bleed on top of that.
Freeze + bleed synergy. Phynx Lv3 deals +50% bleed against enemies with elemental debuffs like ice.
Mymu's Overdraw acts as a revive, buying time for Phynx bleeds to stack. Mymu needs 5-star+ and his skin to be effective.

budget_f2p.note: Cheapest competitive option. Both are rare = easier to star up. Mymu revives, Helix ramps damage when hurt.
Budget option. Mymu revive + Nyanja speed. Both rare and easy to acquire.

best_resonance_combos.important_note: Mymu's Immortal Curse is only effective at 5-star+ with his character skin equipped. Without the skin, the revive mechanic is unreliable.

gold.description: Gold is the primary currency in Archero 2. It has two main uses: buying items in the general store and leveling up gear.
gold.gear_leveling: The main use of gold. Gear levels are tied to the equipment slot, not the individual item. For example, if your boots are level 148, every pair of boots you equip will be level 148 — whether they're Mythic Griffin or Legendary Oracle. This means upgrading gear level benefits any item in that slot. Gets very expensive at higher levels.
gold.general_store: Gold can be used to purchase items from the general store.
gold.profile_level_cards: Gold can also be used to buy profile-level-up cards when you reach each 10th profile level. You can buy 10 cards per level; they are randomly generated (e.g. Health increase, skill refresh, Red heart healing+, speed bonus). This is a rarer, sometimes expensive use of gold.
gold.gear_tiers_vs_levels: Gear tier is specific to the individual piece of equipment (e.g. Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic). Gear level is specific to the slot (boots, weapon, armor, etc.) and applies to whatever item is equipped in that slot.

campaign.overview: Campaign is one of the main PvE modes. Many expert players don't run it often because later levels get very difficult, but for leveling fast or maximizing rewards there are specific strategies.
campaign.farming_drops: To optimize gear, runes, and scroll drops: choose campaign levels that have 50 floors, not the 6-minute or endless versions. 50-floor runs have 5 boss battles (one every 10th floor), so more boss drops per run. 6-minute or endless runs have only 2 boss battles total, so fewer drops per run.
campaign.fifty_floor_types: There are two types of 50-floor campaign levels. One type requires walking through a door to change floors each time. The other type uses the same map for all 50 floors — e.g. Serenity Pool — so you never have to move; you can leave your character in one spot and farm easily. Same-map 50-floor levels like Serenity Pool are ideal for farming.
campaign.profile_exp_note: Campaign is the only way to earn profile experience. See profile_experience category.

profile_experience.description: Profile experience is your general account or profile level, separate from character or hero stars. It is earned only by playing campaign mode.
profile_experience.example: A player might be profile level 59. When you level up, every 10 levels you unlock the ability to buy cards for gold.
profile_experience.cards_per_10_levels: At each 10th profile level you can buy 10 cards for gold. You keep the cards forever. The cards are randomly generated.
profile_experience.card_effects: Card bonuses include things like Health increase, extra skill refresh, Red heart healing+, speed bonus, and many more. Each purchase gives random rolls.
profile_experience.gold_note: Buying these cards uses gold and can be expensive. This is a rarer use of gold compared to gear leveling and the general store.

tracking_eye.name: Tracking Eye
tracking_eye.description: Your projectiles gain the ability to track enemies. Reduces DMG dealt by 10% (doesn't affect Sprites or elemental damage). Reduces main weapon and Strike projectile speed by 50%. Works best with Oracle Staff or when combined with Piercing Arrow or Energy Beam.

custom_facts.text: Guild donations: You can donate 5 times per day. The first donation is free, then costs increase by 20 gems each (free → 20 → 40 → 60 → 80). Donations are how guilds level up.

Runes:
There are 4 different types of equipable runes, etched runes, blessing runes, enhancement runes, ability runes. A player can equip a max of 3 etched, 2 blessing, 4 enhancement and 4 ability at a time with all slots unlocked. Each rune has special abilities based off of its quality and enchantment stats.
